module_title: Literacy, Sex Ratio, and Urbanization - Basic 2011 Census Data
introduction: The quality of a country's human resources is heavily measured by its literacy rate and gender equality (Sex Ratio), while urbanization reflects economic development and industrial transition. At this beginner level, we will rote-memorize the absolute most important national averages and the top/bottom performing states from the 2011 Census.

core_concepts.title: Literacy Rate
core_concepts.description: According to the Census, 'a person aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language' is considered literate. In 2011, India's National Literacy Rate was '74.04%'. 'Kerala' is the most literate state in India (94%), while 'Bihar' is the least literate state (61.8%).

core_concepts.title: Sex Ratio
core_concepts.description: Sex Ratio is defined as 'the number of females per 1000 males' in a given population. It is a prime indicator of the status of women in society. India's National Sex Ratio in 2011 was '943'. 'Kerala' has the highest sex ratio (1084 - meaning there are more women than men), while 'Haryana' has the lowest sex ratio (879).

core_concepts.title: Urbanization
core_concepts.description: This refers to the percentage of a country's total population living in cities or towns. As per the 2011 Census, approximately '31.16%' of India's population lives in urban areas (while 68.84% lives in rural villages). In terms of percentage, 'Goa' is the most urbanized state (62.2%), while 'Himachal Pradesh' is the least urbanized state (only 10.03%).

important_entities.name: Kerala
important_entities.significance: Kerala is the only major state in India that consistently ranks Number 1 across almost all positive demographic and social indicators. Whether it is the highest literacy rate, the highest sex ratio, or the lowest Infant Mortality Rate (IMR), Kerala always tops the list.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam trap: Students often assume literacy is calculated from birth (0 years) or from 5 years of age. This is incorrect. In the Indian Census, literacy is calculated ONLY for populations aged '7 years and above'. All children below 7 years of age are legally classified as 'illiterate', even if they attend school.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Behind in Books = Bihar. Behind in Daughters = Haryana.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Lock in the absolute lowest states: Lowest overall literacy is Bihar. Lowest overall sex ratio is Haryana.

exam_strategy_tips: The three national averages (Literacy 74.04%, Sex Ratio 943, Urbanization 31.16%) must be rote-memorized. They are asked directly in almost every tier-1 exam.
The definition of Sex Ratio ('Females per 1000 Males') is a standard question in basic General Awareness tests.
